Property usage overview

In total, 75 distinct properties are used.

Legend for the tables below:

  • subjects: how many subjects have at least one of this property
  • r_p: the above as a percentage of all subjects
  • dist_objs: the number of different values appearing in this property
  • e_objs: at most seven random sample values of this property
  • n: the total number of appearances of this property
  • objs_per_rec: calculated from the above, the mean number of appearances of this property per subject
  • subjs_with_mult_vals: the number of subjects that have more than one repetition of this property

Harper is part of the Chicago Public Schools district and is named for scholar and educational administrator William Rainey Harper and opened in 1911. The school was named in honor of William Rainey Harper (1856-1906), a legendary educator who served as president of both the University of Chicago and Bradley University, and who was a champion of modernizing the facilities and standardizing the academic curriculum of the Chicago Public Schools] (1)|[It changed its name in 1962? from: Kazanskiĭ veterinarnyĭ institut.] (1)|[Org. in May 1964] (1)|[Mt. Angel College run by the Benedictine Fathers of Mt. Angel opened on the 1st Tuesday in Sept. 1887. Mt. Angel Seminary opened in 1889. Later, the institution was known as Mount Angel College and Seminary and included Mt. Angel College (with courses of study for both boys and men) and Mt. Angel Seminary (with a boys seminary and a mens seminary). By the end of the 1930s, the College and Seminary had separated. Mt. Angel College began accepting women in the late 1930s and closed in 1946. Its prep school for boys continued until the mid-1970s. Mt. Angel Seminary remains, under the auspices of Mt. ## <td headers="e_objs" class="gt_row gt_left">[The Koch family lived in the United States from at least 1890 to 1909.] (1)|[The Frederick Weyerhaeuser family consists of North American descendants of Minnesota lumberman Frederick Weyerhaeuser (1834-1914).  Weyerhaeuser was born in Germany and came to the United States in 1852.  He arrived in Saint Paul in 1891, and was president of the Weyerhaeuser Timber Company; in 1959 the name of the corporation was shortened to Weyerhaeuser Company.  Weyerhaeuser married Sarah Elizabeth Bloedel  October 11, 1857.  The couple had eight children.] (1)|[George Henry Howard married Agnes Poett Howard in 1857. Agnes was the widow of George's older brother, William Davis Merry Howard. George and Agnes had four children together: George Henry Howard, Julia Howard, Agnes \"Babette\" Howard, and Joseph Henry Poett Howard. The family mostly resided on their their El Cerrito Estate, located on the San Mateo Rancho, which William Davis Merry Howard purchased in 1849. George ran the family's cattle and livestock operations.] (1)|[The Swallow family were farmers in Vermont and Illinois. Nahum Swallow (1771-1851) migrated with his wife Deidamia Woods (1778-1858) from Massachusetts to settle in West Windsor, Vermont in 1796. Together they had fifteen children, including Deidamia, Prudence, Nahum, Nancy, Ransom, Eliza, Gardner, Guy, Mary, Chester, Franklin, Olivia, Luthera, John, and Jane. In 1819, Deidamia married Timothy Ladd and Prudence married Asahel North. They moved with their husbands to Illinois, where they began farming. Other siblings later moved to join them in the West.] (1)|[Several of the Fowlers in this line worked in the banking business, including James Thomas \"J. T.\" Fowler, the son of George Fowler, who helped found the Home State Bank in Arcadia, Kansas, in 1908.  James Thomas Fowler began his banking career as cashier and managing officer.  He later helped organize the First State Bank of Arma, Kansas, and served as chairman of the board of directors for both these banks, as well as the Citizens Bank of Weir, Kansas.] (1)|[The Kemper family consists of all descendants of Johann Kemper (ca. 1635-1670 in modern North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany) and Anna Loew. The American line of the Kempers settled in Cedar Grove, Virginia in the early eighteenth century. Prominent members include Reverend James Kemper (1753-1895) and James Lawson Kemper (1823-1895), governor of Virginia from 1874-1878.] (1)|[The Ortega family consists of descendants of Pedro de Ortega and Costáca Juarez Galindo of the Andalusia region in Spain who were active in 1725.  The manuscript depicts a family tree of eight generations of Ortegas including a number of the named individuals in the record of the legal proceedings.] (1)</td>

## <td headers="e_objs" class="gt_row gt_left">[Commandment Keeper Church, Beaufort, South Carolina (May 1940) is a derived title given to unedited field footage held by the Library of Congress in the Mead (Margaret) Collection and Chalfin (Norman and Ethel) Collection when it was named to the National Film Registry in 2005, and by which the film is commonly known. The title is used on the videodisc boxed set, Pioneers of African-American Cinema, for a 16-minute film derived from the Mead and Chalfin footage, with an audio track taken from field recordings also held by the Library of Congress in the Chalfin Collection. That video is also available on several streaming platforms. The title of the field footage and field recordings in the Library of Congress catalog is [South Carolina, May 1940, Commandment Keeper Church, Beaufort].] (1)|[For the past two decades, the Australian National University has had a program for the study of Islam in Southeast Asia. Over the years, this program has produced an impressive array of graduates, many of them from the region, whose theses document the variety and vitality of Islam in Southeast Asia. Because much of this original research has not been readily available to the global community of Islamic scholars, this series of publications is intended to make this research internationally accessible.] (1)|[This distinctive series, developed from special issues of Art History (LCCN 80646761), publishes new work by leading scholars on a full range of key themes and breaking issues for the discipline.] (1)|[In May, 1900 the American Mutoscope &amp; Biograph Co. made numerous \"living pictures\", which were very short films representing well-known works of art. Shot by cameraman, Arthur Marvin, these included Faith\" by Sarony, and \"The Morning Star\" by Sarony. Sarony probably refers to American lithographer and photographer Napoleon Sarony (1821-1896). The company later compiled four living picture films into a single film entitled \"Living pictures\" (also known as \"Living picture production\") which was released in 1903.] (1)|[Chroma was commissioned by The Royal Ballet. Choreography: Wayne McGregor; restaging: Antoine Vereecken; music: Jack White and Joby Talbot; set: John Pawson; costumes: Moritz Junge; lighting: Lucy Carter. First performance: London, Royal Opera House, November 16, 2006; Royal Ballet. First Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater performance: New York, New York City Center, Dec. 2013; Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater.] (1)|[Azad Hind as news magazine founded by and associated with 'Chandra Bose' published in Urdu from Kolkata and English from Saigon).] (1)|[These keepsakes were produced by the publisher for friends, customers etc.] (1)</td>

## <td headers="e_objs" class="gt_row gt_left">[The Kent State University College of Architecture and Environmental Design (CAED) Florence Program offers an opportunity to study abroad in Italy to those students enrolled in the junior year of the Bachelor of Science in Architecture program.] (1)|[The Film Booking Office of America (FBO) was a motion picture production and distribution company. Established in 1920 as the Robertson-Cole Company, it was reorganized as the FBO in 1922. In 1928 the company merged with Keith-Albee-Orpheum to form Radio-Keith-Orpheum (RKO), and its motion picture production business was incorporated as Radio Pictures in 1929.] (1)|[Research &amp; Development Department: Since the re-establishment of Men-Tsee-Khang (MTK) in 1961, MTK has worked consistently in fulfilling its primary objective of preserving, promoting and developing   Tibetan medicine. Even though MTK has always realized the importance of initiating a research study and developing Tibetan Medicine further, her early phase of journey was restricted to preserving the very identity of Tibetan Medicine due to the dire situation and limited resources. MTK was able to stretch further by early 1980 owing to growth of staff and wider infrastructure. Research &amp; Development (R&amp;D) Department was first incepted in 1984 building the initial block of documentation and case studies. Realizing the importance of this department, R&amp;D is branched into three sub-divisions as follows: a) Clinical Research Department   b) Materia Medica Research Department, and c) Herbal Product Research Department] (1)|[Walta Information and Public Relations Center S.C. is a private media outlet and Public Relations Center established in 1994. Its major objective is playing significant roles in minimizing the gap of information flow in the country; Website: www.waltainfo.com  Email: feedback@waltainfo.com  Tel: +251-11-661 12 65  Fax: +251-11-661 25 79  P.O.Box: 12918  Addis Ababa, Ethiopia)] (1)|[Celestron has been an optics industry leader for decades, ever since Tom Johnson unveiled the game-changing C8. We strive to continue his legacy by continually developing exciting products with revolutionary technologies. Here, you can learn all about our patented, one-of-a-kind innovations.] https://www.celestron.com/pages/about-us (2)|[Corktown Cinema in Corktown section of Detroit is an independent art-house cinema formed three years after the Burton Theatre closed.] (1)|[The Four J's were a doo wop vocal harmony group from Philadelphia, USA. Their original line up comprised of Joseph Pirollo a.k.a. Junior (lead), Joseph Paparella (second tenor), Joe Milaro (baritone) and James Testa (first tenor) but soon before they recorded in 1958 Joseph Paparella was replaced by Joseph Pirollo's brother in law Robert Finizio. In 1960 Robert P. Marcucci of Chancellor wanted a vocal group to back up Fabian in the studio recordings and tours, so The Four J's became The Fabulous Four with Joseph Pirollo, Robert Finizio, James Testa and Ernie Spano. In 1963 they renamed again themselves The Four J's adding Johnny October from The Four Dates in their line up, recording their biggest hit \"By Love Possessed\" at Jamie.] (1)</td>

## <td headers="e_objs" class="gt_row gt_left">[Emma Miller is a wife, mother and a grandmother who lives a quiet life in Delaware. She's the author of the Hannah's Daughter's, Amish mystery and Amish Matchmaker series.] (1)|[Eugene Butler worked at the Progressive Farmer Company for his entire life. Eugene received his bachelors from Mississippi State University in 1913, his second bachelors from Cornell University in 1915, and a Masters in agronomy from Iowa State University in 1917. He started as an assistant editor of the Progressive Farmer, an agriculture publication, between 1917 and 1922. His father, Dr. Tait Butler, started the publication as the Southern Farm Gazette in 1895. Eugene worked his way through the company and became its president in from 1964 to 1968. He continued to serve as chairman of the board and editor-in-chief until 1983, when the company was bought by Time Inc. He retired in 1985, but continued to write the history of the company until his 100th birthday.] (1)|[Alan Brown is a freelance artist and graphic designer.] (1)|[Bookseller in London.] (1)|[Emile Marie Laurent (October 1, 1852 - October 1930), was the Prefect of Police of Paris from September 1914 to June 1917.] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89mile_Marie_Laurent (1)|[Riley Smith (born April 12, 1978) is an American actor. He is known for his roles on television, such as recurring roles in the series 24, Joan of Arcadia, 90210, True Blood and The Messengers, and starring roles on the television series Drive and Frequency. In 2019 he was cast to play Ryan Hudson in the CW series Nancy Drew. Riley was born in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, and raised in Marion, Iowa.] (1)|[b. 1949] (1)</td>
